title: Waste awaiting processing
context: A facility receives waste every day. After six days, incoming waste is reduced while processing capacity stays the same. How does the amount of waste awaiting processing change?
assumptions: A single storage site; stock is measured in tonnes (t) and time in days.
Inflow changes once at the intervention boundary. Outflow capacity is constant.
Actual processing is limited by the stock and incoming waste available during each interval; stock cannot be negative.
No storage limit, degradation, or other outflow is represented. This is an educational model.

title: Water stored in an urban area
context: Runoff enters an urban storage area. After six minutes, runoff decreases while drainage capacity stays the same. How does the volume of stored water change?
assumptions: A single water reservoir; volume is measured in m³ and time in minutes.
The input is runoff flow, not rainfall intensity. Rainfall is not converted into runoff.
Actual drainage is limited by the water and incoming runoff available during each interval; stock cannot be negative.
No topography, infiltration, overflow, storage limit, or prediction of flood depth is represented.
